prompt: A ramp-checking app solves $\tan\theta = 1$ for $0^\circ \le \theta < 360^\circ$. One answer is $45^\circ$. What is the OTHER answer, in degrees?
hint: $\tan\theta = \frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}$. If sine and cosine BOTH flip sign, the fraction stays the same.

hints.text: $\tan\theta = \frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}$. If sine and cosine BOTH flip sign, the fraction stays the same.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Test the idea with numbers: $\frac{0.7}{0.7} = 1$ and $\frac{-0.7}{-0.7} = 1$ too. So the opposite direction on the circle gives the same tangent. Opposite means add $180^\circ$.
Add half a turn to the first answer: $45 + 180$.

explanation: Straight across the circle, at $225^\circ$, the point is $(-0.707, -0.707)$. Both parts flipped sign, and two minus signs cancel when you divide.
$\tan 225^\circ = \frac{-0.707}{-0.707} = 1$ as well, so the other answer is $225^\circ$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Tangent is slope
steps: tan θ is the slope of the line from the centre through the point.
A single straight line through the centre passes through the circle at TWO opposite spots, and both share the same slope of 1. Those spots are 45° and 45 + 180 = 225°.

alternativeExplanations.title: Sort by quadrant signs
steps: tan is positive when sin and cos share a sign: both plus (Quadrant 1) or both minus (Quadrant 3).
Quadrant 1 gives 45°. The matching Quadrant 3 angle is half a turn further on: 225°.
